bibliography.abstract: This study develops a survey-calibrated, path-dependent agent-based microsimulation for evaluating crime and violence reduction policies in Bolivia. A synthetic population is constructed from the 2025 Household Survey and the fourth-quarter 2025 Continuous Employment Survey using official expansion weights and cross-survey donor matching. The model combines heterogeneous agents, place-based risk, criminal adaptation, institutional capacity, community organization, and multiple policy channels. Uncertainty is propagated through adaptive Gaussian-process and tree-ensemble emulators, global sensitivity analysis, tempered ensemble MCMC, and predictive meta-calibration. Simulated portfolios include focused policing, community control, Guardabosques-type incentives, social prevention, environmental interventions, justice reforms, investigation, rehabilitation, and financial-network disruption. Results are interpreted as structural policy scenarios rather than causal forecasts, with explicit attention to displacement, distributional effects, implementation capacity, and multi-objective trade-offs.
bibliography.title: A Path-Dependent Agent-Based Microsimulation of Crime and Violence Reduction Policy Portfolios in Bolivia: Survey Calibration, Adaptive Emulator Ensembles, Global Sensitivity, Tempered MCMC, and Multi-Objective Policy Analysis

en.caveats: The simulation results are designed to be interpreted as structural policy scenarios rather than predictive causal forecasts.
en.what: This study develops a survey-calibrated, path-dependent agent-based microsimulation to evaluate crime and violence reduction policies in Bolivia. The model constructs a synthetic population using official expansion weights and cross-survey donor matching from the 2025 Household Survey and the fourth-quarter 2025 Continuous Employment Survey. It simulates heterogeneous agents, place-based risk, and criminal adaptation across multiple policy portfolios, propagating uncertainty through adaptive Gaussian-process and tree-ensemble emulators, global sensitivity analysis, and tempered ensemble MCMC.
en.why: It provides a structural framework to evaluate multi-objective policy trade-offs, displacement, and distributional effects of complex crime interventions under deep uncertainty, rather than relying on simple causal forecasts.
